text:
maria_support: Customer (AcmeSearch) opened a support ticket — their free-trial credits dropped ~11k overnight. They say the job that calls /v1/embeddings ran as usual but cost is off by an order of magnitude. Can someone triage?

alex_infra: Thanks, forwarding their logs now. Do we know which key they used (api key vs service account)?

maria_support: They supplied a project-level key tied to a scheduled worker. They run a nightly fanout that batches 25 items -> embeddings endpoint. Stack traces attached in the ticket show repeated 401s followed by retries. Paste below (redacted):
```
[2026-03-16T02:03:04Z] worker-45 POST /v1/embeddings 401 Unauthorized - token expired
[2026-03-16T02:03:04Z] worker-45 retrying job 1/5 backoff=2s
[2026-03-16T02:03:06Z] worker-45 POST /v1/embeddings 200 OK cost=25 tokens
[2026-03-16T02:03:06Z] worker-45 marking succeeded
[2026-03-16T02:03:06Z] worker-45 ack job
[2026-03-16T02:03:07Z] worker-45 POST /v1/embeddings 401 Unauthorized - token expired (for different batch id)
[2026-03-16T02:03:07Z] worker-45 retrying job 2/5 backoff=2s
[2026-03-16T02:03:09Z] worker-45 POST /v1/embeddings 200 OK cost=25 tokens
```
maria_support: They say visibility/ack semantics look normal on their side. Suspect the worker retry logic lacked idempotency keys so each retry consumed tokens again.

kai_engineer: Looks like a tight loop where failed auth -> immediate retry -> success, but the client doesn't dedupe across attempts. Each success after a 401 still consumes tokens. If the job batched 25 items and retried twice for many batches, cost multiplies. Do we have server-side dedupe for embeddings? Not currently.

alex_infra: We saw a small spike on infra metrics matching their org_id at 02:03. Linked incident: https://infra.redwood/alerts/iv-8271 (sre-bot). The pattern matches auth header refresh failures — perhaps the key rotation triggered short-lived 401s.

zoe_billing: From billing perspective, if calls returned 200 OK then they are billable. But we usually issue credits for customer-impacting auth edge cases. I'd recommend issuing a provisional credit equal to the excess and granting an extra 5k trial buffer while we investigate.

maria_support: Customer asked for repro steps; they shared their worker code. It's a cron job that refreshes service token every 30m and doesn't attach an idempotency header. Snippet:
```js
await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
  body: JSON.stringify({ inputs: batch })
});
```

kai_engineer: Recommended mitigation: add an Idempotency-Key header per input batch and exponential backoff on 401s with token refresh before retrying. Longer term: we'll add server-side duplicate suppression for identical batch hashes when requests succeed within a short replay window (RFC: ENG-2312). I'll open a quickfix PR to require/accept Idempotency-Key for batch endpoints.

alex_infra: Action items: (1) Kai to PR temp server-side replay suppression (ENG-2312), (2) Zoe to issue provisional credit and trial top-up, (3) Maria to tell customer to patch worker with Idempotency-Key and backoff. Who owns the refund ticket?

zoe_billing: I'll create BILL-4891 and apply a credit of 11,250 tokens immediately; will follow up with formal invoice adjustment.

maria_support: Customer updated: they patched the worker to attach uuid v4 idempotency keys and will run one small test batch tonight. They appreciated fast response. Closing loop after PR deploy. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: [alert] infra alert iv-8271 resolved — deploy of auth-cache fix rolled at 2026-03-16T02:20:00Z

kai_engineer: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service/pull/1147 - adds server-side batch dedupe + logs. Will monitor for similar spikes.

maria_support: I'll update the ticket and tag customer with the credit note. Thanks everyone.
